note: Adapted from the species description of Chhotani (1997), originally in English; the alate, soldier and dimorphic worker are described, and the original biological notes are retained; synonymy, literature citations, distribution records and figure numbers are omitted.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule pale yellow to dark yellowish brown; antennae brown, paler at base; labrum brown; mandibles dark reddish black, paler at base. Pilosity of head sparse, of body denser. Body length 3.5–5.10 mm. Head capsule oval, length to base of mandibles 1.15–1.35 mm, maximum width 1.0–1.20 mm, closely resembling O. obesus in shape. Antennae 16–17-segmented; with 16 segments segment 4 shortest, with 17 segments segment 3 shortest. Labrum lingulate, broadly rounded anteriorly. Mandibles long and slender, sickle-shaped, apex incurved, 0.75–0.95 mm long, longer than half head length, mandible length/head length 0.60–0.63. Postmentum moderately inflated, subrectangular, 0.65–0.85 mm long, 0.45–0.58 mm wide. Pronotum saddle-shaped, anterior margin weakly to deeply notched at middle, posterior margin slightly concave, 0.45–0.60 mm long, 0.70–1.0 mm maximum width.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Dimorphic. Major worker: head capsule light yellowish brown; antennae brown, paler at base; body and legs creamy white. Pilosity of head and body rather dense. Body length 3.0–5.20 mm. Head capsule subquadrate, length to base of mandibles 1.20–1.35 mm, maximum width 1.30–1.40 mm. Antennae 17–18-segmented; with 17 segments segment 5 shortest, with 18 segments segment 4 shortest. Postclypeus weakly inflated, nearly half as long as wide. Pronotum saddle-shaped, anterior and posterior margins both distinctly notched, 0.35–0.38 mm long, 0.70–0.80 mm wide. Minor worker: similar to major worker but smaller, antennae 16–17-segmented; body length 3.0–3.8 mm, length to base of mandibles 0.70–0.78 mm, maximum head width 0.85–0.90 mm, pronotum 0.30–0.35 mm long, 0.57–0.60 mm wide.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule light reddish brown to dark chestnut brown; antennae and postclypeus brown, paler than head capsule; pronotum paler than or as dark as head capsule, with paler T-shaped mark and shoulder spots; abdominal tergites slightly paler than head capsule, sternites yellowish brown. Pilosity of head and body dense. Body length 25.0–29.0 mm with wings, 9.2–15.0 mm without wings. Head capsule subcircular, wider than long, length to base of mandibles 1.70–1.85 mm, width including compound eyes 2.30–2.66 mm. Fontanelle minute, circular, slightly raised, the surrounding area flat or slightly concave, not paler. Compound eyes subcircular or broadly oval, maximum diameter 0.70–0.75 mm, minimum diameter 0.60–0.75 mm, adjacent to lower margin of head. Ocelli broadly oval, long diameter 0.25–0.36 mm, short diameter 0.18–0.25 mm, separated from compound eye by about half their short diameter, i.e. 0.12–0.18 mm. Antennae 18–19-segmented; segment 2 longer than segment 3, segment 3 shortest or subequal in length to segment 5. Postclypeus inflated, hairy, half as long as wide. Pronotum trapezoidal, anterior margin slightly raised with a weak median notch, posterior margin weakly incurved at middle, 1.05–1.28 mm long, 2.02–2.43 mm wide. Wings yellowish brown; radial sector trace absent; forewing 24.0–25.0 mm long, hindwing 23.0–24.0 mm long.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: A common species in Sri Lanka and southern India; it damages structural timber and various crops and trees; it builds large, multi-chambered, nearly conical mounds. Swarming occurs in September in eastern India and from November to December in Sri Lanka.
